question: When do ramp vehicles interact with the controlled right-through car, and is abrupt cut-in jerk caused by the comfort request or its realization constraint?
trigger: Sam explicitly requested ramp interaction tests and abrupt cut-in investigation on 29 October, following the retained 33.3704 m/s^3 cut-in failure.
status: Declared before new simulations; development outcomes will be retained, not used to relabel failed cases
ramp_method: Keep all 44 requests, full ramp route and eight ramp departures unchanged; shift only agent_0's requested departure. 0 is the ordinary timing control. Observe actual merge-entry and auxiliary-to-through times, native left-change desire/block flags, and direct ramp/agent_0 leader relations within 120 m. Late timing is synthetic exposure, not an inferred real arrival distribution.
cutin_method: Retain the identical actor, cohort and speed schedule; switch only its lateral request. Diagnostic follow_cap_acc uses min(comfort-filtered, raw ACC follow request), so it knowingly relaxes comfort but never removes SUMO safety. It is not adopted as a new baseline. Compare aligned action/realization traces and actual event timing; no anticipation or future-event metadata is given to any controller.

acceptance.accounting: Every request retained at fixed H and separate drain, zero collision/teleport/removal, all trips complete within drain and controlled physical lanes preserved
acceptance.ramp_exposure: Report separately: every shifted case must contain at least one direct agent_0/ramp leader relationship in sb2/sb3; otherwise label unexposed, not a successful conflict test
acceptance.cutin: Requested cut-in realizes a lane transition and leader relationship; lateral-off control never transitions; both release normally
acceptance.comfort: 2.05 m/s^3 is a reported diagnostic, never a reason to weaken safety; preserve all exceedances
acceptance.repeat: Exact canonical trace plus diagnostic journal identity on one ramp and one cut-in repeat
acceptance.matching: Within each comparison, identical network/demand and safety; no-cut controls differ only in request_lane_change. Compare all seeds, including failed fixtures.

limits: Synthetic uncalibrated demand and provisional geometry. Native desire/block bits are observed timestep states, not independent rejected gap opportunities or human intent. getFollowSpeed equality is mechanism evidence, not a unique identification of internal SUMO safety branches. No learned actor, training, empirical safety/comfort, communication or traffic-benefit claim.
